evidence.proved: BSD-3 control server with no node limit stated
a public headscale instance advertising 'Active Nodes 4 / 5 total' and an authkey join flow, with no service-publishing feature, read through the search index

record.notes: 2026-10-23: public instances exist and carry no ingress. One public control server, headscale.kf8edq.dev, publishes join keys and shows 'Active Nodes 4 / 5 total', so the free public instance is a 5-node control plane with no public listener of any kind. A control plane distributes keys and endpoints; the payload never touches it, which is why headscale cannot satisfy ingress test at any size. Re-graded 2026-10-23: the software is free and the path is not, because it needs a host. The finding is the host.

extras.transit_note: a control server for Tailscale clients: it distributes keys and endpoints and sees no payload
extras.hosting_requirement: a rented or free compute service; no local machine is assumed

record.confidence_note: Control server architecture and mesh coordination specifications are documented in official project documentation.
record.binding_note: the software imposes no byte meter; what runs out is the monthly egress allowance of the host it runs on, and that host is a separate provider
